Layout: where the nodes go

Source: R/mira_pieces.R
mira_layout.Rd

Chooses MiRA's network layout, the one setting that places the nodes. Add it to a plot made with mira(); without it, MiRA uses its default (the bipartite layout for a bipartite network, Fruchterman-Reingold otherwise).

Usage

mira_layout(type, seed, nested)

Arguments

type

One of "fruchterman", "kamada_kawai", "bipartite", "circle", "grid", "random". "bipartite" needs mira(..., bipartite = TRUE).

seed

A whole number. The same seed and the same data give the same node positions, so a figure can be reproduced. Without a seed, a layout that starts from random positions ("fruchterman", MiRA's default for a network that is not bipartite, among them) differs each time the plot opens.

nested

TRUE or FALSE. Bipartite layout only: sort nodes by degree (nested order).

Value

A component, to add to a plot with +.

See also

mira() to start a plot; mira_node(), mira_intralayer(), mira_interlayer() and mira_layer() for the elements it draws.

Other components: mira_camera(), mira_filter(), mira_interlayer(), mira_intralayer(), mira_layer(), mira_legends(), mira_mode, mira_mode_dashboard(), mira_mode_data(), mira_mode_grid(), mira_mode_layer(), mira_mode_map(), mira_mode_meta(), mira_node()

Examples

library(emln)
net <- load_emln(17) # 4 layers; bird and plant nodes
#> Creating state node map
#> Creating extended link list with node IDs
p <- mira(net, bipartite = TRUE, setA_type = "bird")
#> Bipartite network: drawn as undirected. Use directed = TRUE for a directed one.

p + mira_layout("kamada_kawai")
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# The same node positions every time
p + mira_layout("fruchterman", seed = 42)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.

# Bipartite layout, nodes sorted by degree
p + mira_layout("bipartite", nested = TRUE)
#> Not opened: R is not interactive. Print the plot in an R session, or give `browser` to open it from a script.
